name: Routine
subcategory: personal tasks, routines and daily planning
tagline: Combine calendar, tasks, notes, and a command palette into one personal workspace
verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Routine, combine calendar, tasks, notes, and a command palette into one personal workspace. The hard boundary is calendar integrations, cross-platform apps, capture speed, sync, and polish, plus cross-device reliability and workflow polish.
coreLoopDIY: Combine calendar, tasks, notes, and a command palette into one personal workspace, schedule or repeat tasks, work from a focused today view, and keep history locally.
whatYouLose: calendar integrations, cross-platform apps, capture speed, sync, and polish
ongoingBurden: recurrence edge cases, notifications, sync conflicts, calendar APIs, mobile capture, and backups
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Routine because task software is sticky because trust, speed, and ubiquitous capture matter more than the database schema. The recurring cost buys recurrence edge cases, notifications, sync conflicts, calendar APIs, mobile capture, and backups, not just the visible interface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Professional plan and a personal desktop task manager DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Routine in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and desktop notifications; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: combine calendar, tasks, notes, and a command palette into one personal workspace, schedule or repeat tasks, work from a focused today view, and keep history locally.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create inbox, today, upcoming, someday, and completed views with fast keyboard capture.
Support projects, tags, due dates, start dates, priorities, notes, subtasks, and attachments.
Implement robust daily, weekly, monthly, and custom recurring rules with tests.
Add a focus view with one active task, timer, and optional desktop notification.
Provide search, saved filters, undo, and a completed-task archive.
Export and import a documented JSON format and make automatic local backups.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out team assignment and comments.
Deliberately leave out two-way calendar or email synchronization.
Deliberately leave out native mobile apps and cloud accounts.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
